title: Integrated signatures define mutational processes in prostate cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: this paper has no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement listing and no text-mined accessions. The NCBI-linked PMC record (PMC13558581) turned out to be a sister PPCG (Pan Prostate Cancer Group) paper in Nature Communications (Epi2Hit). Its data availability statement says PPCG data are controlled access: raw WGS (whole-genome sequencing) in EGA (European Genome-phenome Archive) study EGAS00001002876, while variant calls and clinical data go only to approved projects via Globus or a secure portal. The panprostate.org home page says data come 'from the European Genome-phenome Archive and by application to the PPCG consortium' via a concept form emailed to ppcg@icr.ac.uk. The EGA study page returns HTTP 200; I did not try to get access.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 959 donors, 8 IMFs (integrated mutational footprints), 6 complex structural-variant signatures, associations with time to metastasis and with response to androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors: all from the abstract only. The metastatic validation uses Hartwig Medical Foundation data, which also needs an application (from a web search result, not checked). Whether the Nature supplementary tables carry per-donor signature exposures together with outcomes is unknown: the supplement could not be retrieved because the paper is paywalled and has no PMCID.

a1_downloadable.note: Controlled access. Raw WGS is in EGA EGAS00001002876, and variant calls plus clinical data need an approved PPCG concept-form application (confirmed in the sister paper's data statement and on panprostate.org). Hartwig metastatic data also needs an application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files available. The outcome labels (time to metastasis, response to treatment) sit in controlled clinical data, and the IMF exposures come from the authors' own signature extraction.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked. The inputs (mutation catalogues per donor) are derived from controlled-access WGS.

a5_enough_rows.note: Abstract says 959 donors, and the unit is the donor. That is under the 1,500-row regression bar and marginal even for classification once restricted to donors with metastasis follow-up. I saw no rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; raw WGS is terabyte-scale, per-donor signature tables would be small

a8_label_provenance.note: IMF labels are themselves outputs of a de novo signature-extraction model (matrix factorisation) run on the same mutations. Predicting them from mutation features would be circular. Only the clinical outcomes are true measurements, and they are controlled access.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached. The data can't be accessed without a consortium application.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the mutation patterns in a prostate tumour's genome to predict how soon the cancer will spread and whether hormone therapy will work.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-donor counts of mutation types (single-letter changes, small insertions and deletions, copy-number changes, structural rearrangements) from whole-genome sequencing of 959 prostate cancer donors (abstract figure, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: Time to metastasis, and sensitivity to androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors (drugs that block the male-hormone receptor), both taken from the consortium's clinical follow-up records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Urologists and oncologists could use a risk score built from the tumour genome to decide who needs more aggressive treatment, but this is only buildable with controlled clinical data.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not assessed (reject). Similar outcome-linked prostate WGS cohorts (Hartwig, ICGC/PCAWG) are also controlled access.

ml_idea: Predict time to metastasis from per-donor mutational-signature exposures, using held-out cohorts or countries as the split. Not feasible without a PPCG data-access application.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the data can't be accessed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether the Nature supplementary tables publish per-donor IMF exposures alongside time-to-metastasis. If they don't (most likely, given the consent restrictions), the project is dead without an application.

verdict_reason: Fails A1. Per-donor variant calls and clinical outcomes from the PPCG (Pan Prostate Cancer Group) are controlled access: raw genomes are in EGA EGAS00001002876, and everything else needs a consortium concept-form application. The paper has no open full text or retrievable supplement. Its signature labels are also model outputs (A8), and 959 donors is a small number of examples (A5).
